Is there really no compulsion in Islam? A new book, edited by Cato Senior Fellow @AkyolinEnglish, brings together a team of Muslim scholars to address this question. 

📚 Order your hard copy of “No Compulsion in Religion—No Exceptions” now!  

Amazon: ow.ly/4T7m50YcnBT  
Barnes & Noble: ow.ly/Ci6250YcnBY  
Bookshop: ow.ly/YhlY50YcnBQ  
Apple Books: ow.ly/qI9g50YcnBS  

🔗 Or download a free PDF thanks to Cato Books:

The federal government wants more Americans wearing health trackers—but your data may not be protected. A new analysis by Cato’s @dr4liberty and @PGEddington warns these devices can collect deeply personal information—and much of it falls outside existing privacy laws. 

ow.ly/vJ5O50YxOQj

Illegal immigrants are about 44% less likely to be incarcerated than native-born Americans, and legal immigrants are 75% less likely to be incarcerated than natives, the 2024 data show. 

Check out the new research by Cato’s @AlexNowrasteh and Michelangelo Landgrove: ow.ly/FORm50YyQ3y

Free enterprise is what makes America exceptional. If we want to meet the AI moment, we need more free enterprise in the electricity sector, says Cato’s @ts_fisher.

Video

People often assume that immigrants are more likely to commit crimes than native-born Americans, especially illegal immigrants. However, this perception is not supported by facts. Evidence shows that illegal immigrants are less crime-prone than native-born Americans.  

Check out the new research by Cato’s @AlexNowrasteh and Michelangelo Landgrove: ow.ly/bp8b50YyOE3

A lot has been said about migrant crime, but the data show that immigrants, both legal and illegal, are significantly less likely to be incarcerated. Check out the new research by Cato’s @AlexNowrasteh.

Video

AI is already helping people when they can’t see a doctor. But current FDA rules about what these tools are allowed to do can stifle care. Easing those rules or lifting them completely could safely widen access to timely, affordable care for millions of Americans.

ow.ly/P9Wz50YybnK

Join the Cato Institute for a conversation with MacArthur Fellow and National Humanities Medalist @platobooktour about her latest book, “The Mattering Instinct: How Our Deepest Longing Drives Us and Divides Us.” nitter.net/i/broadcasts/1pKkOyaRO…

The four major US war aims in Iran are secure. Meanwhile, costs are mounting—oil prices up, LNG markets disrupted, and political and economic costs growing. 

In this article, Cato’s @JustinTLogan outlines a framework for ending the war:
ow.ly/XOER50YyGew

America’s strength is free enterprise—and our energy future depends on bringing that freedom to the electricity sector. Before the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, Cato’s @ts_fisher testifies that rethinking the grid through the lens of economic liberty is key to meeting the AI moment.

Watch the hearing here: ow.ly/hrLZ50YyEjL

Section 230 shapes how online platforms host and moderate users’ speech. Weakening 230 would undermine free speech, innovation, and safety tools, and especially harm smaller online outlets. 

cato.org/blog/senate-approac…

Join the Cato Institute for a policy discussion on Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 and congressional tariff authorities. 

Featuring Cato’s @clark_packard, Representative @RepJimmyPanetta (D CA), @stanveuger of the American Enterprise Institute, and Former Chief of Staff for Representative Ron Kind (D WI), @hana_leah. 
  
🗓️ March 26 | 3 PM EDT 
📍 Cato Institute 
  
Register: ow.ly/ELwY50Yx2OJ

The Cato Institute’s senior fellow in health policy studies, @dr4liberty, will speak in an @Liberal_Studiess webinar on March 27 at 12 p.m. EDT. The topic:  “Canada vs. US Health Care: More Similar Than You Think”. 

Register here: 
ow.ly/WfN350Yyn1x

Remembering Brian Doherty, historian of the libertarian movement and editor with @reason magazine. 

“His impact on the libertarian movement and on libertarian ideas is well known, but that’s not all he impacted,” writes Ivan G. Osorio. 

ow.ly/yUZ150Yyl25

Minnesota lawmakers are weighing whether to carve AI out of the free speech protections in their state constitution. It's a troubling sign of state lawmakers responding to AI fears by threatening core liberties, says Cato's @KevinTFrazier. 
ow.ly/yJja50YxPp5

The government loses about 4 cents per dollar on student loans, says Cato’s @Gillen_Andrew_J. It shouldn’t be the lender at all, he adds, but at minimum, it shouldn’t be losing (or making) money on them. 

Learn more: ow.ly/r40950YxQaa

Video

Director of Energy and Environmental Policy Studies at the Cato Institute, @ts_fisher, will testify before the Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources on “The State of the Bulk Power System,” Wednesday, March 25, at 9:30 a.m.
